verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026, at 6:35:12 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)'; R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission is set to launch on April 1, 2026'; R4: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time, and location directly stated in R1; supported by R2 and R4.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission carries four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew size 4 ... approximately ten-day trip'; R3: 'The crew includes Commander Reid Wiseman ... four astronauts'; R5: 'approximately 10-day test flight'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Crew size of four and ~10-day duration explicitly confirmed across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will fly a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'free-return trajectory around the Moon ... looping around the far side before naturally returning'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in R1 as the mission trajectory.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will perform a lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crewed lunar flyby mission ... Closest approach April 6'; R2: 'looping around the far side of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as a lunar flyby in R1.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT) ... Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Exact location and local date/time match (April 10 PDT).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II lunar flyby is expected around April 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Specific date for flyby/closest approach directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, Jeremy Hansen'; identical in R2-R5
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list confirmed across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as first crewed lunar mission since 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft ... validate the Orion spacecraft's systems'; R3: 'first mission with crew aboard ... Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly a test flight for crewed Orion operations.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS)'; R3: 'first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Described as testing SLS with crew for the first time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II spacecraft will loop around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'looping around the far side'; R2: 'looping around the far side of the Moon'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory goes further than any human has traveled since Apollo 13.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set the record ... breaking Apollo 13's record of 248,655 miles'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states it surpasses Apollo 13 record.

verifications.claim: Backup launch windows for Artemis II are available throughout early April if the launch cannot proceed on April 1.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'seven two-hour launch windows ... 1–6 and April 30'; R2: 'next available launch window dates ... April 2: 6:22 pm CDT April 3: 7:00 pm CDT April 4: 7:53 pm CDT April 5: 8:40 pm CDT April 6: 9:36 pm CDT April 30'
verifications.reasoning: Backups explicitly listed for early April days after April 1.
